prompt: Set up logging for the new payment service. What should I use?
output:
Your team already uses structured logging with correlation IDs across services. Match that pattern:

**Use `kotlin-logging` + `logstash-logback-encoder` (JSON to stdout → EKS picks it up)**

```kotlin
// build.gradle.kts
implementation("io.github.microutils:kotlin-logging-jvm:3.0.5")
implementation("ch.qos.logback:logback-classic:1.4.14")
implementation("net.logstash.logback:logstash-logback-encoder:7.4")
```

```xml
<!-- src/main/resources/logback.xml -->
<configuration>
  <appender name="STDOUT" class="ch.qos.logback.core.ConsoleAppender">
    <encoder class="net.logstash.logback.encoder.LogstashEncoder"/>
  </appender>
  <root level="INFO">
    <appender-ref ref="STDOUT"/>
  </root>
</configuration>
```

```kotlin
// Correlation ID propagation (match the pattern from other services)
class CorrelationIdFilter : Filter<ILoggingEvent>() {
    override fun decide(event: ILoggingEvent) = FilterReply.NEUTRAL
}

// In your gRPC interceptor
MDC.put("correlationId", request.header("x-correlation-id") ?: UUID.randomUUID().toString())

// Usage in any class
private val logger = KotlinLogging.logger {}

logger.info { "Payment initiated" }  // → {"message":"Payment initiated","correlationId":"...","level":"INFO",...}
```

For the payment service specifically, also log these fields on every transaction:
- `paymentId`, `accountId` in MDC (not inline) so they appear on all subsequent log lines in the request
- Never log raw amounts or card data — mask anything sensitive at the logger level

This stays consistent with your existing services, keeps dependencies minimal, and JSON-to-stdout is native for EKS log forwarding.
